config.notes: SPEC COMPLIANCE MILESTONE REVIEW - 30 chunks completed. All review findings were remediated and verified before returning control to the outer orchestrator.

issues.summary: C++ HighBoundary/LowBoundary precision-0 exponent numeric text returned unnormalized text such as 1e2 instead of 100.
C++ dateAddQuantity/dateSubtractQuantity accepted huge finite Quantity values and cast them to integer intervals.
C++ HighBoundary/LowBoundary accepted malformed date and DateTime bodies by slicing fixed positions without full lexical validation.
C++ cqlTimezoneOffset accepted invalid or non-digit timezone offsets such as +99:99 and +aa:bb.
C++ DateTimeValue::parse accepted timezone offsets without the required +/-HH:MM form.
C++ date quantity arithmetic formatted year-precision date strings as DateTime markers such as 2025T.
C++ quantityToInterval converted invalid, empty, or null Quantity JSON to 0 days instead of NULL.
C++-only/browser ToQuantity lacked numeric and Boolean overloads that the Python surface supports.
C++ boundary numeric classification accepted non-finite or overflow text and emitted invalid boundary strings.
Python Quantity/scalar multiply and divide used plain CAST for dynamic scalar operands, accepting valueString numerics and throwing on invalid strings.
Python static Integer overflow handling relied on DuckDB TRY around raw arithmetic, allowing promoted out-of-range integers.
Python Power and ^ lowered to bare POW, yielding NaN for invalid domains instead of NULL and failing arithmetic typing in conformance expressions.
Python _decimal_boundary_text expanded unbounded exponent strings and could allocate massive fixed decimal text.
Python boundary helper timezone validation accepted colonless offsets; tightening required Now() timestamp offset normalization for DuckDB CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.
